reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms after two Codex changes, rebased on the other-harness batch. Empty wakes: the Codex UserPromptSubmit hook now blocks a Notifai wake prompt (with or without its token) when nothing deliverable waits for the session, because the session closed since the wake was queued, another process now hosts it, or the input was already handed in; Codex then starts no turn and makes no model request, and the User sees one 'Blocked by hook' line. A human prompt is never blocked, and a wake with staged input is handed in as before. The Codex reference now tells the agent that a wake that still reaches it with an empty notifai receive asks for nothing, so it ends the turn without resuming earlier work. Codex app and IDE conversations: Codex runs SessionEnd with reason other both for a close and for an unload. For a thread whose rollout originator is the Codex app or the Codex IDE extension, the SessionEnd hook hands the decision to the hub that attends the session; after a short confirmation delay the hub ends the session if the rollout was archived or deleted, if the host app-server has exited, or if the host is not that client's own app-server, and otherwise keeps it open (dormant-open): questions stay answerable, no lease is renewed, and an answer waits as one content-free wake in that thread's own queue, which Codex starts only when the conversation is loaded again. The hub decides the same way when Codex stops the session child of such a conversation without running SessionEnd. The hub stays to watch the app while something waits, so quitting the app still expires the questions. The hub also ends a Codex session whose rollout is archived while loaded, since Codex runs no SessionEnd then. The Codex reference and README say this. CLI conversations, hook definitions, hook output for every other prompt, readiness states and domain terms are unchanged; nothing starts, loads or resumes a closed session. Earlier on main, kept (the other-harness batch, reviewed in its own change): Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and harness references, harness setup and update hand-off, CLI readiness text and domain terms for the other-harness batch, rebased on the session child and hub. OpenCode: the generated plugin offers OpenCode's own question form to the User's devices through `hook opencode-question` and settles it in-process with OpenCode's question API; harness-opencode.md gains a Question form section (do not also register the form with ask; a device answer's acknowledgement arrives in the next system context; an OpenCode answer needs nothing; dismissal or closing the session withdraws it), and guidance is resolved once per User prompt, which harness-opencode.md, updates.md, the update hand-off and the OpenCode doctor contract now say. Grok: route requalified live on 1.0.62 with no behaviour change; the doctor contract and harness-grok.md say closing the session ends its questions. Hermes: writes go through ctx.inject_message aimed at the tracked session and are held during approval prompts and session-switching commands; harness-hermes.md and the Hermes contract say an accepted write is admission, not reading. OpenClaw: a changed plugin is applied to a running Gateway with `openclaw plugins reload notifai` and readiness requires the loaded generation; a reload keeps sessions open while stopping the Gateway or disabling or uninstalling the plugin ends them and expires their questions, which harness-openclaw.md and the README now say; the update hand-off and ask failure text were updated. No domain term changed.
